facts.fact: UNDP Liberia says the online Crime Statistics Information System launched at Liberia National Police headquarters on 25 January 2021 is part of a web-based rule-of-law case management system in which institutions record reported crimes and cases as they move through the criminal justice chain.

UNDP Liberia says the system went live at Liberia National Police headquarters on 25 January 2021 with a five-day training of trainers for 15 personnel, and is to be piloted separately by each institution at first; it names no station or county using it.

UNDP Liberia says the system is an initiative of the joint UN Liberia Rule of Law Programme, led by UNDP and supported by the UNDP Crisis Bureau, as at its launch on 25 January 2021; no domestic funding is stated.

systems.owner: Liberia National Police, under the joint UN Liberia Rule of Law Programme led by UNDP

systems.system: Rule of law case management system
systems.country_label: rule of law case management system / case tracking tool
systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Liberia National Police, piloted separately by each institution
systems.tiers: major rule of law institutions; no tier stated

note: The document also says the system is to yield crime statistics, court backlog and pre-trial detention figures; it states no station-level entry.
